clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with low blood pressure despite a three‑drug antihypertensive regimen, chronic anemia of unknown cause, and multiple cardiovascular risk factors (obesity, Black race, prediabetes, borderline LDL). These findings collectively point to overtreatment of hypertension as the most likely current issue, while anemia, silent CAD, OSA, early CKD, and metabolic syndrome remain important concurrent considerations. Gaps in renal function data, iron studies, orthostatic vitals, and cardiac imaging limit certainty for several diagnoses, prompting a targeted work‑up.

recommended_workup: Serum eGFR and urine albumin‑creatinine ratio (CKD staging)
Complete CBC with differential, ferritin, iron, TIBC, reticulocyte count, vitamin B12, folate
Orthostatic blood pressure measurements and medication‑adherence questionnaire
STOP‑BANG questionnaire followed by home sleep apnea test or polysomnography if indicated
Resting 12‑lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiogram (evaluate LVH, diastolic function, HFpEF)
Coronary artery calcium scoring or stress testing for silent CAD
Lipid panel repeat with non‑HDL and ApoB if needed; consider initiating moderate‑intensity statin per ASCVD risk
Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) and thyroid antibodies
Abdominal ultrasound with liver enzymes to assess NAFLD
Pelvic exam, menstrual history, and pelvic ultrasound if iron‑deficiency suspected
Ankle‑brachial index to screen for peripheral arterial disease
PHQ‑9 and GAD‑7 screening for depression/anxiety
Age‑appropriate cancer screening (colonoscopy, mammography, cervical cytology) as indicated
